title: How PepsiCo brands are turning up in unexpected ways on restaurant menus
summary: PepsiCo is tapping into culinary creativity and brand fandom to transform portfolio favorites into fresh, unexpected food experiences on restaurant menus. Learn more about how PepsiCo are turning up in unexpected ways on restaurant menus.
body_markdown:
PepsiCo food brands and flavors are no strangers to the snack aisle, but lately, they’ve been showing up in places consumers might not expect. Doritos are tucked under shawarma proteins at Osmow’s or piled high as nachos at Subway, and Flamin’ Hot seasoning is adding heat to boneless chicken wings at Kroger and Circle K. Familiar favorites are having a full-on menu moment, giving people new ways to experience the brands they already love.


Across restaurants, franchises, retailers and quick-service menus, PepsiCo foods and flavors, including Flamin’ Hot, Doritos and other portfolio favorites serve as a key element of surprising food experiences. They are being reimagined as enticing menu items built for real meal occasions.


The strategy starts with listening. PepsiCo teams look at consumer demand, social media chatter, search trends and food service insights to understand what people are already experimenting with. Then they work with their in-house chefs and restaurant partners to transform those insights into mouthwatering menu offerings and bring emerging flavor ideas to life. That’s how a flavor mashup or recipe remix that gains traction among fans can evolve into a menu item.


At about 1,000 Kroger stores across the country and at Circle K locations nationwide, Flamin’ Hot Boneless Chicken Wings bring the fiery heat of crowd-favorite Flamin' Hot flavor to the hot food section. This bold culinary innovation taps into a growing consumer interest in hot and spicy protein, making it a crowd-pleaser for summer get togethers and gameday gatherings. The Flamin’ Hot boneless wings will expand to other retail outlets in September.
